chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'I drove the sacrificial animal, and I performed the pairing (Qiran).' He said, 'And why did you do that? The Tamattu' is superior.'
Then he said, 'It will suffice you therein with one circumambulation of the House and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa.'
And he said, 'Circumambulate the Ka'bah on the Day of Sacrifice.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately)
key_terms.قَرَنْتُ: I performed Qiran (pairing Umrah and Hajj together)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qiran and Tamattu' in Hajj, and what are the required rituals for each?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Qiran, where a single Tawaf and Sa'i suffice for both Umrah and Hajj, contrasting it with the superior status of Tamattu'. The specific instruction to perform Tawaf on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) highlights the ritual flexibility granted to the Qiran performer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (taysir) within obligatory acts. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing the procedural nuances between the major forms of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence.
